scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

interpretation_history.interpretation: The dispute volume rose from ~600 tickets in June/July to ~1,200 tickets in August/September, confirming a roughly two‑fold increase since August.

The CRM shows dispute response times are well within the SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs 3‑day SLA) with 2,440 tickets recorded, indicating that response speed is not a current problem despite the high dispute volume.
Route completion for August‑September is 0.88, below the 0.95 target, indicating a gap in the field manual read process that could lead to estimation substitution and incorrect bills.
The observation shows that the tariff change log contains no records, indicating that tariff changes are not a source of the recent dispute surge.

The observation shows that disputed bills are more often associated with actual reads (1785) than estimated reads (1240), indicating that estimation substitution is not the primary driver of the dispute surge.

structural_remedies.description: Audit the billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES) and revert any changes made after July to the pre‑August baseline; enforce a change‑control review before future rule updates.
structural_remedies.rationale: Auditing DA-RULES and rolling back config can be completed within the remaining 225 minutes; requires Billing Operations approval (K-BILLWRITE) but does not involve automated bill writes.; residual gap: Unknown data corruption or other sources (U-ALTERNATIVE-DATA-CORRUPTION) may still cause incorrect bills; already‑issued incorrect bills would need manual adjustment.

structural_remedies.description: Institute a mandatory validation and approval step for any billing import validation rule change, documented in DA-RULES, with sign‑off by SH-BILL before deployment.
structural_remedies.rationale: Defining the process is a lightweight configuration/process change achievable well within the time budget; does not violate K-BILLWRITE or K-DISPATCH.; residual gap: Does not correct historical bills that were already generated with the faulty rules; those remain as a residual gap requiring manual review/adjustment.
